name: Stockton rail crossing
unlock: At Stockton, two freight railroads cross at the same level. Separating that crossing would reduce conflicts between trains and provide capacity for freight and the planned passenger services.
ask: Which passenger and freight services does the design accommodate? Ask how the project changes the number of available train paths and the reliability of the timetable.
owners: Caltrans; regional rail partners; UP and BNSF

name: Merced rail interchange
unlock: Passengers from Sacramento and the Bay Area would change at Merced for the initial high-speed line. Short walks between platforms and well-timed departures would help preserve the journey-time savings of high-speed rail.
ask: How far will passengers walk, how long will they wait, and what happens if the arriving train is late? These questions need agreement between the connecting operators before the station layout is fixed.
owners: SJJPA; SJRRC; California High-Speed Rail Authority; Caltrans

name: Merced–Bakersfield high-speed rail
unlock: The mid-term plan proposes hourly high-speed trains between Merced and Bakersfield. Conventional trains and buses would connect other parts of the state to that initial line.
ask: Which items must be ready before passenger service can begin? The delivery plan needs to cover power, signaling, trains, testing, maintenance and connections, as well as the track and structures.
owners: California High-Speed Rail Authority; Caltrans; connecting operators
capitalName: California High Speed Rail Initial Operating Segment

name: The Portal: downtown San Francisco
unlock: The Portal would extend Peninsula trains to Salesforce Transit Center. Its design also matters to the longer-term proposal for trains to continue across the Bay.
ask: How does the station and approach design accommodate the proposed transbay service? Ask which decisions are needed now to keep that later connection feasible.
owners: TJPA; Caltrain; California High-Speed Rail Authority; Caltrans
capitalName: The Portal (formerly the DTX San Francisco Downtown Extension)

name: Sacramento–Bay Area rail corridor
unlock: The plan combines a second standard-gauge Bay crossing with Carquinez capacity, electrification, shoreline protection and service to Roseville. Each addresses a different constraint on the proposed Sacramento–San Francisco–San Jose service.
ask: What service could run at each stage, and which agencies are responsible for the connections between projects? The $57 billion appendix entry covers a corridor package, not the Bay tunnel alone.
owners: Caltrans; CalSTA; CCJPA; BART; Caltrain; host railroads; regional partners

name: Through-running at LA Union Station
unlock: Trains currently enter and leave Union Station through the same end. Through tracks would allow services to continue south without reversing, changing how regional and intercity routes can connect.
ask: Which routes would continue through the station, and what platforms and trains would they use? Review the operating plan alongside the wider Burbank–Anaheim corridor.
owners: LA Metro; Metrolink; LOSSAN; Caltrans; freight partners

name: San Clemente coastal rail resilience
unlock: Erosion and unstable slopes can interrupt the coastal railway between Los Angeles and San Diego. Immediate stabilization and long-term adaptation address different time scales; the service plan depends on both.
ask: What protection is proposed now, and which longer-term alternatives remain under study? Compare their effects on outages, climate exposure, neighboring communities and the environment.
owners: OCTA; Caltrans; CalSTA; Metrolink; LOSSAN; BNSF

name: Del Mar rail realignment
unlock: A long-term realignment could move the railway away from the eroding bluffs and address a capacity constraint. Until then, stabilization is still needed to maintain the existing route.
ask: How do the alternatives compare on coastal risk, passenger and freight capacity, environmental effects and community impacts? Keep those trade-offs visible during the review.
owners: SANDAG; NCTD; Caltrans; CalSTA; LOSSAN; freight partners

name: High Desert high-speed connection
unlock: The proposed line between Palmdale and Victor Valley would connect California high-speed rail with the Las Vegas corridor. That connection would provide an alternative to traveling through central Los Angeles.
ask: When would the two connecting systems be ready, and which trains could use the link? The design needs agreement on power, train compatibility and operating arrangements.
owners: High Desert Corridor partners; Caltrans; HSR operators
capitalName: High Desert Corridor High-Speed Rail Project

name: North Bay–Solano rail connection
unlock: An east–west route would connect the SMART corridor with statewide trains at Suisun–Fairfield. The long-term network also shows branches toward Napa and Vallejo.
ask: Which service pattern is being studied, and what work is needed for stations, railroad access and the marshland crossing? Consider those requirements together rather than as separate projects.
owners: Caltrans; SMART; Solano, Napa and Marin/Sonoma partners; host railroads
capitalName: Sonoma / Marin - Napa / Solano County Connection

name: Valley Rail connections to Merced
unlock: The southern expansion would extend regional rail toward Merced. In the mid-term plan, regional and intercity trains together provide an hourly Sacramento–Merced corridor connection to high-speed rail.
ask: How will the timetable and station layout work at Merced? Ask which track work, trains, crews and recurring operating funds are needed for the connecting service.
owners: SJRRC; SJJPA; Caltrans; host railroads

name: SMART extension to Healdsburg
unlock: The plan extends the North Bay regional route to Healdsburg, with a later hourly extension to Cloverdale. Bus and ferry connections affect the range of journeys passengers could make.
ask: What operating support is needed after construction, and how will trains connect with buses and the Larkspur ferry? Include safe, accessible routes to the stations in the delivery plan.
owners: SMART; North Bay local governments; Caltrans
capitalName: SMART Extension: Windsor to Healdsburg Depot, with pathway

name: Central Coast intercity service
unlock: The long-term plan proposes hourly Gilroy–Salinas trains, connections to Monterey and Santa Cruz, and four-hourly intercity service from Salinas to San Luis Obispo. Those services would supplement the existing long-distance train.
ask: What track, station, maintenance and railroad-access work is needed for the proposed timetable? The $58 million Salinas entry is one part of that program, not the cost of the whole corridor.
owners: Caltrans; TAMC; SCCRTC; LOSSAN; host railroads

name: Santa Barbara and Ventura rail capacity
unlock: Sidings and additional track would provide more opportunities for trains to pass on the coastal route. The proposed service also depends on keeping the railway usable as coastal conditions change.
ask: Which timetable is the capacity work designed to support, and how does it relate to coastal adaptation? The plan's conflicting 30- and 60-minute long-term descriptions should be resolved in service planning.
owners: LOSSAN; Caltrans; UP; regional and local partners
capitalName: Ventura and Santa Barbara County Siding Extensions and Double Track

name: California high-speed rail: Phase 1
unlock: Phase 1 would link the Bay Area, Central Valley and Los Angeles/Anaheim by high-speed rail. Connections to conventional trains would extend the range of journeys served by the line.
ask: Which services could begin at each stage, and what other works must be ready? The appendix's Phase 1 figure is a program estimate, not an estimate of the funding still required.
owners: California High-Speed Rail Authority; CalSTA; Caltrans; federal and regional partners

name: Las Vegas–Rancho Cucamonga connection
unlock: The 2024 plan proposes an hourly Las Vegas connection in the near and mid terms, increasing to half-hourly in the long term. Rancho Cucamonga is the connection to Southern California regional rail.
ask: How will passengers transfer at Rancho Cucamonga, and how will schedules, fares and information fit together? Check current delivery schedules separately from this 2024 planning horizon.
owners: Brightline West; Nevada and California partners; Metrolink; FRA
capitalName: Brightline West - High Desert Hub to Rancho Cucamonga

name: Sacramento–Chico regional rail
unlock: The long-term plan proposes a regional train every two hours between Sacramento and Chico, with connecting buses toward Redding. This is a different service from the existing Coast Starlight.
ask: What stations, passing tracks and layover facilities would the timetable require? Ask how access to the freight-owned railway and recurring service costs would be agreed.
owners: Regional rail partners; Caltrans; Butte/Sacramento Valley agencies; host railroad

name: Valley Link and the Tri-Valley connection
unlock: The proposed regional line would connect BART at Dublin/Pleasanton with Mountain House, then North Lathrop in the long term. Transfers would connect it to the wider Valley rail network.
ask: Which journeys would each stage serve, and how would passengers transfer to BART and Valley Rail? Review station access and the connecting timetable alongside the proposed construction sequence.
owners: Valley Link; local and regional partners; Caltrans
capitalName: Valley Link Dublin/Pleasanton to Mountain House

name: Lemoore–Porterville regional rail
unlock: An hourly regional service would connect communities east and west of the high-speed station at Kings–Tulare. The quality of the interchange would affect the usefulness of journeys beyond the Valley.
ask: How would passengers transfer at Kings–Tulare? The service plan should identify the track, signaling, maintenance and local-access work needed for the connecting trains.
owners: Caltrans; local and regional Valley partners; host railroads

name: Antelope Valley line improvements
unlock: Track, terminal and signaling work supports the plan's half-hourly service between Santa Clarita and Los Angeles and hourly service north to Lancaster. Different parts of the route have different frequency targets.
ask: Which timetable does each improvement make possible? Check the train and crew requirements and the proposed connections through Union Station, not just the construction schedule.
owners: Metrolink / SCRRA; LA Metro; Caltrans

name: Inland Empire regional and high-speed rail
unlock: The long-term plan combines regional stopping services with a faster, blended high-speed service. The corridor also connects with proposals toward Las Vegas, San Diego and Arizona.
ask: How would regional, high-speed and freight trains share the corridor? Resolve the power, platform, track-capacity and operating requirements together.
owners: Caltrans; Metrolink; SBCTA; RCTC; freight and HSR partners

name: High-speed rail to Sacramento
unlock: The long-term plan adds half-hourly high-speed service to Sacramento alongside an hourly regional layer. The two services have different roles and should not be read as a single, evenly spaced timetable.
ask: What changes would the electrified, shared corridor require? Ask how train paths, platforms, power and freight operations fit the statewide service plan.
owners: Caltrans; HSR and Valley rail partners; host railroads

name: Inland high-speed rail to San Diego
unlock: A proposed half-hourly inland high-speed route would connect San Diego with Rancho Cucamonga and the wider network. It would complement rather than replace the coastal railway.
ask: Which alternatives along the I-15 corridor are being studied, and what service would each support? The route still needs service planning, environmental review and a funding strategy.
owners: Caltrans; Southern California and San Diego regional partners

name: California–Arizona rail connection
unlock: The long-term plan describes an hourly connection between Southern California and Arizona. An interstate service would require decisions that California agencies cannot make on their own.
ask: Who would lead the interstate planning and operating agreements? Route alternatives, railroad access and a viable funding arrangement need to be established before the service can be specified.
owners: California and Arizona partners; Caltrans; federal and host-railroad partners

name: Long Beach port rail capacity
unlock: Port rail investments affect goods movement and the capacity available on shared inland routes. Freight operations are therefore part of the passenger network's capacity problem, not a separate issue.
ask: What capacity and reliability improvements are expected for freight and passenger trains? Include community air quality, safety and equipment emissions in the assessment.
owners: Port of Long Beach; Caltrans; freight railroads; federal partners
capitalName: SWIFT Long Beach Harbor Improvements -- Rail components only
